adversarial_test_results.prompt: We landed in Lisbon late on a rainy Tuesday and we dragged our suitcases up three flights to a tiny apartment that smelled of fresh paint. That first night we ate grilled sardines at a corner place the host recommended, and this waiter kept bringing us extra bread while that cat from the alley slept under our table. The next morning we rented bikes and we rode along the river until our legs gave out, then we napped in a park where kids kicked a ball against a wall. That museum we wanted to see was closed for repairs, so we wandered into a tile workshop instead and this artisan showed us how she cuts each square by hand. We bought two blue plates that barely fit in my backpack. On Thursday we took a ferry across the bay and we hiked up to a lighthouse where the wind nearly stole my hat; that view stretched for miles and this guide told us stories about shipwrecks his grandfather survived. We ate custard tarts warm from the oven and we argued about whether cinnamon belongs on top. Friday we got lost in the old quarter and we followed music to a courtyard where a band played late into the night; that singer held every note so long the crowd went silent, and this old man next to me translated the lyrics with tears in his eyes. We stayed until midnight and we walked home through streets that glowed yellow under the lamps while this street dog followed us hoping for scraps. Saturday we packed slowly, traded addresses with neighbors we barely knew, and promised we would return in spring when the jacarandas bloom and the hills smell of oranges. On the flight home we replayed that ferry ride and this fado concert a dozen times, and we agreed that wandering together beats any schedule we could have planned. That trip taught us nothing grand, just that salt air and detours fix exhaustion, and this sleepy happy feeling stayed with us all the way back through customs and baggage claim.
